canonical_name: Brown representability theorem for generalized cohomology
canonical_statement: Intended theorem family: a reduced generalized cohomology theory on a suitable pointed CW homotopy category, satisfying the source's exact wedge and excision/Mayer-Vietoris hypotheses, is represented degreewise by pointed spaces; compatibility with suspension may assemble the representing spaces into an Omega-spectrum. The statement phase must determine from the primary source whether the canonical root is Brown's functor-level theorem, this cohomology-theory consequence, or a compatible spectrum-valued strengthening.
domain_and_universes: Open: the pointed homotopy category of connected pointed CW complexes or the exact source category, a Set/pointed-Set/Ab-valued contravariant functor, and the universes needed for hom-sets, coproducts, and representing objects.
quantifiers: a contravariant homotopy functor h on the exact source category
or a graded reduced generalized cohomology theory h^n, if that is selected as the root
all objects and indexed wedges covered by the source hypotheses
hypotheses: homotopy invariance or passage to the homotopy category
the exact wedge axiom, including its variance and permitted indexing size
the exact excision, Mayer-Vietoris, or weak-pushout exactness condition used by the selected source theorem
any connectedness, pointedness, CW-type, smallness, and coefficient hypotheses required by the source
conclusion: There exists a representing pointed space Y with a natural equivalence h(X) equivalent to pointed homotopy classes [X,Y], degreewise in the cohomology-theory formulation; any claimed Omega-spectrum compatibility requires additional checked structure.
statement_choices_requiring_source_audit: Brown's general contravariant functor theorem versus its generalized-cohomology corollary
connected pointed CW complexes versus a broader CW homotopy category
pointed sets versus groups or abelian groups as the codomain
wedge and Mayer-Vietoris/excision axiom formulations and indexing size
degreewise representing spaces versus a coherently assembled Omega-spectrum
